title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 5

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the fault-description lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The electrical maintenance tutor will review fault-description vocabulary on Friday at ten thirty. Students should meet in the classroom next to the laboratory and bring the sample maintenance report. The lesson will compare the terms intermittent, damaged, loose and unavailable. Students will practise describing an observation without guessing its cause.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which document should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The electrical maintenance tutor will review fault-description vocabulary on Friday at ten thirty. Students should meet in the classroom next to the laboratory and bring the sample maintenance report. The lesson will compare the terms intermittent, damaged, loose and unavailable. Students will practise describing an observation without guessing its cause.

tasks.prompt: A maintenance note stated that a display sometimes became blank during normal use. The technician recorded when the problem occurred and described the visible behaviour. The note did not claim that a particular component had failed because further checks were required. This distinction helped the next technician understand what had been observed and what still needed investigation. Reading 1. What behaviour did the technician record?
Why did the note avoid naming a failed component?
options: Further checks were needed before the cause could be confirmed

tasks.prompt: The display ___ blank during normal use, according to the report.
Choose TWO features of a useful fault description.
options: A guess presented as a confirmed cause
When or under what conditions it occurred

tasks.prompt: A problem that occurs sometimes but not continuously is described as ___.
You have observed an intermittent problem but do not know its cause. What should you write?
options: The control unit is definitely faulty.
The display became blank twice during the observation period; the cause has not been confirmed.
The system is broken because I think so.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of fault description in a logical order.
options: Pass the information to the responsible person
Record when or under what conditions it occurred
correctOrder: Record when or under what conditions it occurred
Pass the information to the responsible person

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing an electrical fault for a maintenance report. Include the observed behaviour, when it occurs and what remains unconfirmed.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
